task_retrieval_key:
A 78-year-old woman underwent DMEK surgery. Four weeks after the procedure, mild opacification in the graft-host interface was observed. Visual acuity rehabilitation stopped at 20/50 in the affected eye, although the graft was attached and stromal thickness had returned to normal (552 μm). Six months later, the patient complained about blurred vision.
Examination revealed:- Graft detachment caused by a paracentral opaque mass- Enlargement of the abnormality - Pseudohypopyon formation- Increased visual impairment at 28 months follow-up
